summary: The candidate correctly enables by default the existing safe decode-lock skip and passes its focused unit tests. This mitigates exhaustion caused specifically by redundant decode-held Mamba snapshots. It does not address the broader original contract of scheduler progress under unsatisfiable Mamba admission/eviction, and it supplies no serving-path responsiveness regression. Independent testing still finds a no-reclaim allocation failure when states remain admission-locked, so this is a partial fix rather than a full resolution.

tests.what_was_measured: Nine pre-existing boundary tests passed. A separate source import showed the base default and effective SGLANG_OPT_MAMBA_SKIP_DECODE_LOCK values were False. Raw output: /job/review-evidence/base/mamba-ratio.log and /job/review-evidence/base/default-env.log
Ten tests passed, including the candidate's assertion that the option defaults on and existing locked-versus-evictable pool boundaries. Raw output: /job/review-evidence/candidate/mamba-ratio.log
Nine streaming-session lock receipt and state lifecycle tests passed. Raw output: /job/review-evidence/candidate/streaming-session.log
Seventeen allocation-aware eviction tests passed. Raw output: /job/review-evidence/candidate/allocation-eviction.log

Independent boundary invocation: a 2x pool reclaimed a decode-evictable prefix, a 2x pool with admission-locked prefixes failed allocation after eviction was attempted, and a 3x locked pool succeeded. Raw output: /job/review-evidence/candidate/adversarial-boundaries.log
A fresh process observed candidate default True and effective False, verifying the documented rollback escape hatch. Raw output: /job/review-evidence/candidate/override-zero.log
The candidate's committed streaming-session evidence log has trailing whitespace at line 29; source changes themselves showed no whitespace error.

gpu_execution.evidence: The interpreter detected one AMD Instinct MI350X with ROCm gfx950 and imported the checked-out source. No GPU execution is claimed as issue evidence because the candidate changes CPU-side policy and the required H100 TP=8 hybrid-Mamba serving workload and weights were unavailable. Raw environment output: /job/review-evidence/candidate/import-and-gpu.log

remaining_counterexamples: At candidate commit, a 2x Mamba pool with all prefix states admission-locked still cannot reclaim a slot and raises 'Can not alloc mamba cache' after eviction is attempted.
The candidate has no bounded-progress or fail-fast behavior for a request whose Mamba demand exceeds the pool, a case explicitly reported in the original issue discussion.
The post-flush case reported with zero running requests is not explained by redundant decode-held locks and has no candidate regression.
No test demonstrates that /health or completion handling stays responsive while admission cannot make progress.
Direct hierarchical-cache I/O blocking, the original 222-second TTFT, and TP=8 behavior remain untested.
remaining_limitations: Only one AMD gfx950 GPU was available, not eight H100 80GB GPUs; CUDA, TP=8, production traffic, and multi-node behavior are unverified.
The deterministic tests cover cache allocation and lock-state mechanics, not full HTTP scheduler responsiveness, direct HiCache I/O latency, EAGLE, or model semantics.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
